primitives.name: Union of Outer Regular Sets
primitives.verbatim_quote: The union of a sequence of outer regular sets is outer regular; the union of an increasing sequence of inner regular sets is inner regular.
primitives.assumptions: Sets are defined in a locally compact Hausdorff space with finite measure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When the union exceeds finite measure, outer regularity may fail.

layer2.mapping: GSI employs outer regular approximations for posterior probability bounds; GSE models state evolution via increasing sequences of inner regular sets.
layer2.telemetry: Convergence of measurable approximations to target sets.

primitives.name: Intersection of Inner Regular Sets
primitives.verbatim_quote: The intersection of a sequence of inner regular sets of inite measure is inner regular; the intersection of a decreasing sequence of outer regular sets of finite measure is outer regular.
primitives.assumptions: Each set in the sequence has finite measure and is inner regular.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when measure becomes infinite or sets lose regularity.

layer2.mapping: GSI infers lower bounds via decreasing inner regular approximations; GSE tracks system states through nested intersections.
layer2.telemetry: Stability of inner approximation under intersection.
